summary: Navigation to somewhere else. Renders an <a> when given `href`, a <button> otherwise.
useWhen: the interaction takes the user to a different page, view or resource
the destination should support middle-click, open-in-new-tab and copy-link

useInstead.when: the interaction changes something rather than going somewhere
useInstead.why: a link that does not navigate breaks middle-click, open-in-new-tab and the screen-reader announcement all at once

useInstead.when: it is a primary navigation destination in a header or sidebar

inline.use: the default — a link inside a paragraph. Underlined in every state, because a link in body copy must not rely on colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1)

standalone.use: a link that already reads as interactive from its position — a card footer, an action row. Underlines on hover only

startIcon.note: omit Icon's `label` — the link text already names it

endIcon.note: the external-link or arrow affordance; same rule about `label`

a11y.role: link when `href` is set, button when it is not
guarantees: the rendered element follows what the caller is actually building, so the announcement is always honest
`inline` stays underlined in every state, so it never depends on colour alone
requires: link text that makes sense read on its own — screen-reader users navigate by a list of links

antiPatterns.dont: "click here" or "read more" as the whole link text
antiPatterns.why: out of context in a links list it names nothing

antiPatterns.dont: adding a size prop or wrapper to scale it
antiPatterns.why: a link is inline and inherits its type from the text around it, by design — icons are sized in `em` to follow

antiPatterns.dont: `target="_blank"` with no warning in the text or endIcon
antiPatterns.why: an unannounced new tab disorients screen-reader and low-vision users
